arms.note: One run, to confirm end to end that the limitations section is stripped before the final gate. Three repeats are wasted on a binary question; this is the cheapest run that can answer it.

queries.text: Across the retrieved papers, what methods do recursive language model systems use to aggregate information that exceeds a single context window, and how do they differ in where the aggregation happens?
queries.note: The same query again, so the answer family -- a taxonomy with a limitations list -- is the one that produced the aggregate/claim disagreement in three earlier passes.
